key_insight: Power-law measurement spectra preserve a benign optimization landscape but can create an optimizer-dependent precision wall when weak-direction curvature falls below the effective denominator floor.
engineering_relevance: Optimizer denominator precision can limit recoverability in low-rank matrix sensing even without spurious local minima, making numerical floors a practical design constraint.
method: Analyze rank-D Burer–Monteiro matrix sensing with covariance Σ = diag(j^−s).
Derive leading-order non-gauge curvature scaling as V^−(s+1)D^−s and an optimizer-specific critical exponent.
Calibrate Adam’s detection lag on four configurations, then freeze it for held-out evaluation.
evidence_signal: The calibrated formula predicts Adam’s onset within 0.45 in the critical exponent across all 16 held-out V × D configurations and distinguishes pairs with equal VD.
watch_item: The approximation fails at D = 2 and saturates at a dynamical floor below ε₀ = 10^−8, limiting extrapolation to small rank or smaller denominator floors.
paper_title: The Precision Wall: An Optimizer-Dependent Boundary for Optimization under Power-Law Measurement Spectra
